summary: Crash when clicking "Presets" after setting the superflat preset with a non-existent biome
description: Crash when you click "Presets" after replacing the "minecraft:plains" to a non-existent biome in the superflat customization menu I was creating a world called "Nether" with Superflat, I replaced "minecraft:plains" to "minecraft:the_nether" to see if the piglins won t turn to zombified piglins, I clicked "Done" and clicked "Presets" again to see if "minecraft:the_nether" doesn t has turn onto "minecraft:plains" again, and The Game Crashed What I expected to happen was: When I click presets after replacing it, it should resets to default. What happened was: It crashed after I press presets. How to reproduce: Create a new world in Superflat click on Customize, after click on Presets replace the biome from "minecraft:plains" to a non-existent biome in the superflat customization menu after click on Done and Presets again and see if it crash(If you press cancel it won t crash)
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Create a new world with Superflat.
2. Click on "Customize" in the world creation menu.
3. In the customization menu, click on "Presets".
4. Replace the biome from "minecraft:plains" to a non-existent biome (e.g., "minecraft:the_nether").
5. Click "Done" to apply the changes.
6. Click "Presets" again in the customization menu.
7. Observe that the game crashes after clicking "Presets".
Environment: Minecraft Java Edition Versions: 1.16.2, 1.16.3 Release Candidate 1, 1.16.3, 1.16.4 Pre-release 1, 1.16.4 Pre-release 2, 1.16.4 Release Candidate 1, 1.16.4
Observed Behavior: When attempting to click "Presets" after setting the superflat preset with a non-existent biome, such as changing "minecraft:plains" to "minecraft:the_nether," the game crashes. This occurs when creating a new Superflat world named "Nether," customizing it by replacing "minecraft:plains" with "minecraft:the_nether," and then clicking "Done." Upon subsequently clicking "Presets" again, the game crashes instead of resetting to default settings as expected. To reproduce this issue, create a new Superflat world, click on Customize, replace the biome from "minecraft:plains" to a non-existent biome in the superflat customization menu, and then click Done followed by Presets again. If you press Cancel instead, the game does not crash.
Expected Behavior: When clicking "Presets" after replacing the biome with a non-existent one, the game should reset the superflat customization settings to their default values without crashing. This should allow the user to revert changes and avoid any unexpected errors or interruptions in world creation.
